IY-03.title: Why a Snow-Blocked Tailpipe Can Kill You Before the Cold Does
notes:
Haseeb's notes (reply to v1, 2 Nov): "The scenes don't match the script. You need to redo this."
What he means, concretely: v1 and v2 narrate things the pictures never show. Scenes 4-7 put a roadside blizzard in "forest_night", show digging out the tailpipe as the "build" pose, and the narration mentions headlights passing and a farmhouse 60 steps away that are never on screen. Rewrite the episode so EVERY scene literally shows its narration with the available sets, props and poses: stay in the "snow" set (the car prop beside the character) for the whole roadside story, use poses that match each action (crouch or kneel by the car to clear snow, sit to wait, shiver in the cold, lookout to watch, signal or wave to get attention), and change any beat that cannot be drawn (for example, drop the passing headlights and the farmhouse, and build the twist from what is on screen). Keep the topic and the two true rules: stay with the car in a whiteout, and clear the tailpipe before running the engine because of carbon monoxide.

EH-02.title: How Does a Cyclone Form, and Who Gives It a Name?
notes:
Haseeb's notes (2 Nov, 18:21 Oslo): fix the dated lines so the episode stays correct after Cyclone Murasu makes landfall (expected the night of 2-3 November) and for as long as it is on YouTube.
- Do not describe Murasu as "approaching", "closing in", "now severe" or with a "now forecasts" wording. Use the past tense and anchor every Murasu fact to a date: e.g. "In early November 2026, Cyclone Murasu formed in the Bay of Bengal..." and "As of 2 November, India's weather office forecast landfall winds of 100 to 110 km/h, gusting to 120."
- Replace "last week's Cyclone Arnab" with a dated phrase (e.g. "Cyclone Arnab in late October 2026") and keep its figures.
- Update the title, description and opening lines the same way (no "is closing in"). The hook can still open on Murasu as a recent storm.
- Keep everything else (structure, explanations, sources, length). Re-check any changed fact.
